claude_proposed_widenings.name: soul_displacement
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Magic Jar's primary mechanic is the caster's soul vacating the body and inhabiting a physical container. This is not an 'activate' procedure on a target — it is the caster themselves becoming a disembodied soul stored in an object. The caster's body becomes an independently-vulnerable catatonic entity. No existing family (ongoing_effect, activation, triggered_reaction, anchored_trigger) represents a procedure where the agent of the spell is displaced into an item anchor.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Your body falls into a catatonic state as your soul leaves it and enters the container you used for the spell's Material component.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: possess_creature
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Possession is not command_companion (that is for summoned creatures the caster controls externally). Possession replaces the caster's in-world stat block with the host's physical stats while the caster retains mental/class stats. It also simultaneously displaces the host's soul into the container. No existing effect atom captures this mutual soul-swap with stat-block overlay.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Your soul enters the target's body, and the target's soul becomes trapped in the container. Once you possess a creature's body, you control it. Your Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Speed, and senses are replaced by the creature's.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: apply_stat_override
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Mid-spell replacement of a specific subset of the possessor's statistics (HP, HD, STR, DEX, CON, Speed, senses) with the host's values while retaining all other statistics is not modify_ac, modify_speed, or any existing effect atom. It is a selective stat-block substitution unique to possession-class effects.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You otherwise keep your game statistics. [implying STR/DEX/CON/Speed/senses/HP are replaced by the host's, while spells, proficiencies, saves, etc. remain the caster's]

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Duration.permanent_until_dispelled
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Magic Jar's duration is 'permanent (ends: dispel)' — it persists indefinitely without concentration and without a timed window. The existing Duration union only has instantaneous, concentration (with upTo DurationValue), and timed (with a fixed DurationValue). A fourth variant is needed for spells that persist until externally ended (Alarm also uses this pattern, but was approximated with timed in its encoding).

claude_proposed_widenings.name: dual_entity_container_state
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: At any point during the spell, the container may hold zero, one, or two souls (caster's soul while body is empty; target's soul when caster is possessing; both when caster returns). Each soul has independent mobility constraints and death conditions. The existing anchor/lifecycle atoms have no representation for a container as a multi-occupant soul repository with per-occupant rules.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If another creature's soul is in the container when it is destroyed, the creature's soul returns to its body if the body is alive and within 100 feet. Otherwise, that creature dies.
